small_guidance:
- The current kernel is dominated by the 128×32768×32768 GEMM; sweep larger tiles (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32, BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64) with num_warps=8 and num_stages=4 to better hide K-loop loads. Add a GROUP_M block swizzle (=8) so adjacent N tiles share L2 reuse of the small (M=128) X matrix.
- Pre-transpose weight to (K, N) contiguous once at init so the inner B load is contiguous along N rather than strided-loading via `tl.trans(w)` every iteration; this halves load latency on the hot K loop.
- Avoid the two-launch + best_config readback: fix BLOCK_N (don't autotune over it) or size `partial` from META in the grid lambda, and fuse the partial-tile sum directly into a single atomic add into a per-row scalar so the reduce kernel disappears.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a split-K / persistent GEMM where each program owns a (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N) tile, performs bias-add + pairwise max-pool + sum across its N tile in registers, and atomically accumulates a single fp32 scalar per row into the output (scaled in the epilogue). Eliminates the partial buffer and the second kernel entirely.
- With M=128 only, prefer a tall-skinny layout: BLOCK_M=128 (covers all rows in one program-m), grid only over N tiles, persistent over the K loop with num_stages=4. This maximizes weight reuse and removes M-tiling overhead.
- Consider fp16/bf16 accumulation of x and W into tl.dot (cast on load, keep fp32 accumulator) — RTX 4090 tensor cores give ~2× throughput, and the 5e-2 tolerance easily covers the precision loss.
